```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(randomForest)

tidymodels_prefer()

```
```{r}
# Column names are kept exactly as they appear in the CSV.
marks <- read_csv("data sheet 3.csv") |>
  mutate(Trace.Type = factor(str_to_lower(Trace.Type)))  # console: glimpse(marks)
```

```{r}
#| label: split

# 80/20 split, stratified by mark type
set.seed(459)
marks_split <- initial_split(marks, prop = 0.80, strata = Trace.Type)
marks_train <- training(marks_split)
marks_test  <- testing(marks_split)
```

```{r}
#| label: boxplots

# Measurements only: drop the two character columns, then reshape long
marks_train |>
  select(-`Experimental Context`, -Effector.Char.1, -Effector.Char.2) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Trace.Type,
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "measurement"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Trace.Type, y = measurement, fill = Trace.Type)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(vars(feature), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Trace type", y = "Measurement (log10 scale)", fill = "Trace type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: baseline

# Share of the training marks in each class
class_props <- 
  marks_train |>
  count(Trace.Type) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) # show in console

baseline_accuracy <- round(max(class_props$prop), 2)
```

Baseline accuracy is `r baseline_accuracy`.

```{r}
#| label: recipe

# Trace.Type is the outcome; the text columns become metadata, leaving the 12 measures as predictors
marks_rec <- # console: marks_rec to check that the number of predictors is 12
  recipe(Trace.Type ~ .,
        data = marks_train) |>
  update_role(all_nominal_predictors(),
              new_role = "metadata")
```

```{r}
#| label: rf-one

# Model specification: a random forest with 500 trees, 3 measures tried per split.
# We reuse this model spec for most of the lab.
rf_spec <- 
  rand_forest(mtry = 3, trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("randomForest",
             importance = TRUE) |>  # needed for the importance plot
  set_mode("classification")

# Fit recipe + forest to the whole training set
set.seed(459)
rf_one <- workflow(marks_rec,
                   rf_spec) |>
  fit(marks_train)

rf_engine <-  # console: look at rf_engine
  extract_fit_engine(rf_one)
```

```{r}
#| label: rf-one-accuracy
#IS THE MODEL ANY GOOD AND HOW DO WE KNOW?
# Compare each training mark's OOB prediction with its true label
oob_accuracy <-
  accuracy_vec(truth = marks_train$Trace.Type,
               estimate = rf_engine$predicted)
```

Out-of-bag accuracy of our model is `r round(oob_accuracy, 2)`

```{r}
#| label: rf-one-importance
#WHICH MEASURES MATTER MOST?
# Gini importance from the fitted forest, reshaped long and sorted largest first
rf_engine$importance |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "feature") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(feature, MeanDecreaseGini),
             y = MeanDecreaseGini)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Mean decrease in Gini") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: rf-one-trees
#HOW MANY TREES ARE ENOUGH?
# OOB error after each of the 500 trees, reshaped long and plotted
rf_engine$err.rate |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(tree = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -tree,
               names_to = "class",
               values_to = "oob_error") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tree, y = oob_error, colour = class)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Number of trees",
       y = "Out-of-bag error",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: cv

# Deal the training marks into 10 folds, stratified by mark type
set.seed(459)
folds <- vfold_cv(marks_train, v = 10, strata = Trace.Type)

# Accuracy (many others available)
marks_metric <- metric_set(accuracy)

# Same forest as above; train on 9 folds and test on the 10th, ten times; keep the predictions
cv_fit <- workflow(marks_rec, rf_spec) |>
  fit_resamples(folds,
                metrics = marks_metric,
                control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE))

# Scores averaged over the 10 folds, then the confusion matrix of all out-of-fold predictions
collect_metrics(cv_fit)
collect_predictions(cv_fit) |> conf_mat(Trace.Type, .pred_class)
```
